what: Encode of the decoded twitter.json value through test_binding into a new std::string per iteration, under five settings of glibc malloc.
why: The encode arms of 2026-10-04-074304Z had two modes, near 700 and near 1450 MiB per second. This run asks where the modes come from.
how: One binary (g++, the new arm of that run), encode_tree alone, 12 repetitions per setting. default and default2: no tunable. threshold: GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.mmap_threshold=16777216. toppad: glibc.malloc.top_pad=67108864. notrim: mmap_threshold=16777216 and trim_threshold=268435456.
finding: Without a tunable each repetition reads the slow mode; with top_pad or a high trim threshold each repetition reads the fast mode. The string of the writer grows to 400 KB in each iteration and is freed at its end; glibc gives the top of the heap back to the system, and the next iteration takes fresh pages. The library is not the cause.
